text.en: Meena stirred sugar into water and then sand into water. "One disappears, the other settles," she said.

Matter is classified into pure substances and mixtures. An atom is the smallest unit of an element that takes part in a chemical reaction. A molecule consists of two or more atoms bonded together. In a molecular substance such as water, each molecule represents the characteristic bonded group of atoms. When two or more elements combine chemically, the new substance is a compound.
A homogeneous mixture has a uniform composition throughout a sample. A heterogeneous mixture varies from place to place, even when its different regions are small. Mixtures are separated by methods suited to the parts: sublimation, solvent extraction, simple and fractional distillation, centrifugation and chromatography.
A solution is a homogeneous mixture. A solute is dissolved in a solvent, which often supplies the medium and is present in the larger amount. Solutions may be solid, liquid or gas. Suspensions and colloids are heterogeneous mixtures whose particles are bigger.

A molecule consists of two or more atoms bonded together. In a molecular substance such as water, each molecule represents the characteristic bonded group of atoms.
When two or more elements combine chemically, the new substance is a compound.
A homogeneous mixture has a uniform composition throughout a sample. A heterogeneous mixture varies from place to place, even when its different regions are small.
Mixtures are separated by methods suited to the parts: sublimation, solvent extraction, simple and fractional distillation, centrifugation and chromatography.
A solution is a homogeneous mixture. A solute is dissolved in a solvent, which often supplies the medium and is present in the larger amount.
Solutions may be solid, liquid or gas.
A stone and the air in a room both have mass and occupy space. Their different behaviour makes them different kinds of matter, but both meet that definition.

board.text: Matter has mass and occupies space

text.en: Compare iron and oxygen. Each is an element because all its atoms have the same number of protons. An element cannot be separated into simpler substances by ordinary chemical changes.
An oxygen molecule contains two atoms of the same element. A water molecule contains atoms of hydrogen and oxygen bonded together. A molecule and a compound are different ideas.
Table salt is a compound that forms an ordered arrangement of ions. Its formula shows their simplest ratio. Some pure substances consist of atoms or ions in structures instead of separate molecules.
Compare water with sugar dissolved in water. Every water molecule has the same atom ratio. Sugar water can have different proportions depending on how much sugar was dissolved.

A teacher’s diagram can compare clear salt water and muddy water. In clear salt water the dissolved material is distributed uniformly. Muddy water may have different amounts of suspended matter in different places.
A solution of sugar in water can look clear because the dissolved material spreads through the water at the molecular scale. Ordinary filter paper does not remove that dissolved sugar.

board.text: Dissolved substances can pass through ordinary filters

text.en: A suspension can settle when left still. In contrast, a colloid contains particles small enough to stay dispersed for much longer in a typical sample.
In a diagram with a narrow light beam, some colloids make the beam’s path visible by scattering light. This is called the Tyndall effect. A true solution does not normally show it in the same way.

Milk is an emulsion, a colloid with tiny liquid droplets dispersed in another liquid. Oil and water shaken by themselves can separate again. The arrangement depends on how well the droplets stay dispersed.

board.text: Emulsion: droplets dispersed in a liquid

text.en: Brass is often used as an example of a solid solution of zinc in copper. Air is a mixture of gases, and salt water is a liquid solution. The state of a solution can vary.
In a liquid solution, a solute can be a solid, liquid or gas. Dissolved carbon dioxide in a fizzy drink is an example of a gas distributed through a liquid.

board.text: Gas in liquid: carbon dioxide in a drink

text.en: A separating technique works by using a difference between substances. Use a sieve for size differences between dry pieces, or a filter when insoluble pieces are too large to pass through its pores.

After muddy water stands, some particles settle. Pouring off the liquid above them is decantation. Further separation can remove more suspended material, but clear appearance is not a test of drinking safety.
In the textbook diagram of a centrifuge, rapid spinning separates some parts based on how they move in the spinning mixture. A dairy can use this idea to separate cream from milk.
Some solid substances pass directly to vapour under suitable conditions. In a separation diagram, a substance that sublimes can leave behind a solid that does not sublime under those conditions.

Oil and water are immiscible and can form layers. The layer positions reflect their densities. In another technique, solvent extraction moves a dissolved substance preferentially into a suitable separate liquid.
A distillation diagram shows a liquid becoming vapour and cooling back into liquid. This can recover water from a salt solution while most of the dissolved salt remains behind.
When two miscible liquids have close boiling points, a fractionating column allows repeated vaporisation and condensation. These stages can improve separation compared with one simple stage.
In paper chromatography, a solvent moves through paper and carries some dissolved dyes. Different interactions with paper and solvent cause the spots to travel different distances.

board.text: Different travel distances show a separation

text.en: Choose a separation by stating what you want to recover. Salt crystals can remain after water evaporates. To collect the water instead, the vapour must be cooled and condensed.
Finish by classifying a sample, then choosing the property you can use. Ask whether the composition is uniform, what state each part is in, and whether you want one or several separated parts.

board.text: Classify → identify useful property → choose a method

problem.en: A mixture contains insoluble sand and dissolved salt in water. Which steps can recover the sand and then the solid salt?

text.en: Filter the mixture to collect the sand on the filter.

why.en: Sand particles are insoluble and large enough to be held by a suitable filter.

text.en: Allow water in the filtered solution to evaporate.

why.en: The dissolved salt passed through the filter and can remain as crystals after evaporation.

prompt.en: A friend says A compound is just a mixture of elements. How will you reply?

requiredIdeas.en: A compound is formed by a chemical combination of elements.
A mixture keeps the properties of its parts.

points.en: Matter is pure substance or mixture.
Mixtures can be homogeneous or heterogeneous.
